title: John Lennon watches Ann Peebles perform in Los Angeles | 1974
content:
John Lennon and May Pang watched Ann Peebles perform at the Troubadour in Los Angeles, USA, on 12 January 1974.

Peebles had recently scored a hit with ‘I Can’t Stand The Rain’, and was midway through a week-long residency at the Troubadour which started on 8 January. Al Wilson was the support act.

Lennon and Pang were joined by guitarist Jesse Ed Davis, his partner Patti Daley, and Jim and Cynthia Keltner. They first dined at Lost On Larrabee, becoming customarily intoxicated, and Lennon went to the toilets and emerged with a Kotex sanitary towel on his head.

Upon their arrival at the club, Lennon asked a waitress, “Do you know who I am?” She hit back with “Yeah, you’re some a*****e with a Kotex on his head.”

Ah, y’want the juice… If I’d said, ‘Do you know who I am?’ I’d have said it in a joke. Because I know who I am, and I know she knew, because I musta been wearing a Kotex on me head, right? I picked up a Kotex in a restaurant, in the toilet, and it was clean and just for a gag I came back to the table with it on me head. And ’cause it stuck there with sweat, just stayed there, I didn’t have to keep it on. It just stayed there till it fell off. And the waitress said, ‘Yeah, you’re an a*****e with a Kotex on,’ and I think it’s a good remark and so what?
John Lennon
Rolling Stone, 5 June 1975

After leaving the Troubadour, Lennon, Pang, Davis and Daley went to the Villa Sevilla duplex apartment owned by Lennon’s lawyer Harold Seider. There, things got even messier. While Lennon was in the kitchen, Davis had approached him on all fours and bit Lennon’s torso. Lennon reacted by hitting Davis with a Coca-Cola bottle, which left the guitarist unconscious.

Daley screamed in shock, but Lennon showed that Davis was not dead by pouring orange juice on his head to rouse him. Daley’s screams, however, led to armed LAPD officers attending the property. They left after realising that Lennon was among the drunken guests.
